operators.encoding_note: p_brand and p_container are dictionary-encoded (uint8_t); resolve dictionary codes for 'Brand#23' and 'MED BOX' at init time and compare integer codes

operators.description: Single pass over shared lineitem scan. For each row where l_partkey matches: (a) accumulate SUM(l_quantity) and COUNT(*) into per-partkey aggregation array, (b) append (l_partkey, l_quantity, l_extendedprice) to materialization buffer

outputs.agg_array: direct_array keyed by l_partkey: {sum_qty: double, count: int64}
outputs.mat_buffer: vector<tuple<int32, double, double>> of (partkey, quantity, extendedprice)

operators.description: For each matching partkey, compute threshold = 0.2 * (sum_qty / count). Store in threshold_array[partkey]
Iterate materialized buffer, apply per-partkey quantity threshold, accumulate sum of extendedprice

data_structures.mat_buffer: vector<struct{int32_t partkey; double quantity; double extendedprice;}>

step1_part_scan.reason: Part table is 2M rows, dictionary filter is trivial; single-thread completes in <5ms

step2_lineitem_consume.notes: Shared scan delivers morsels. Each thread has thread-local agg_array and mat_buffer. Bitset check is read-only shared. After scan, merge thread-local agg_arrays (add sum_qty, count) and concatenate mat_buffers.

step3_thresholds.reason: Only ~2000 active entries in agg_array; iterate bitset to find them

step4_final_agg.notes: Partition concatenated mat_buffer across threads. Each thread produces partial sum. Final reduce merges partial sums.

indexes.purpose: Not used; sequential scan with dictionary filter is faster for 2M rows

join_order.notes: Bitset indexed by p_partkey (250KB, fits in L3 cache). Probe is a single bit-test per lineitem row — zero hash overhead. Equivalent to a semi-join that also materializes matching rows.

aggregation: two_phase: (1) streaming per-partkey avg via direct_array during scan, (2) post-scan scalar SUM with threshold filter over materialized buffer
notes: Q17's correlated subquery requires knowing AVG(l_quantity) per partkey before filtering, preventing a pure streaming approach. The decorrelation strategy uses a single pass over the shared lineitem scan with a ~50MB memory footprint: accumulate per-partkey statistics and materialize the ~60K matching rows (~1.5MB buffer), then post-scan compute thresholds and apply the final filter+aggregate over the small buffer. The part filter (Brand#23 + MED BOX) is extremely selective (~0.1%), making the bitset semi-join nearly free. Thread-local aggregation during the shared scan avoids contention.
